It says accurate placement can improve performance while using less space than conventional approaches. Bedrock has drilled at nine sites so far and operates in several US states and Alberta.

segments.title: A possible link to data-centre demand
segments.body: Bedrock says it has spoken with data-centre developers interested in using geothermal systems for cooling or to reduce pressure on the electricity grid. Its CEO told TechCrunch that freeing up several megawatts could allow one data centre to operate earlier. The company plans to use the new funding to add rigs and enter more regions.

content.headline: ULA rocket fails to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit
content.shortHeadline: ULA launch failure leaves 40 Amazon satellites short of orbit
content.standfirst: United Launch Alliance says an anomaly about 10 minutes into a Vulcan flight prevented it from delivering 40 Amazon Leo satellites. The cause is unclear, and the mission was the first of 38 launches Amazon had purchased from ULA.

sources.originalTitle: Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites

segments.body: United Launch Alliance says its Vulcan rocket suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes after launch and failed to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. The company said it did not yet know what caused the failure and would investigate.

segments.title: A setback for the launch plan
segments.body: The mission was due to be the first of 38 flights Amazon had purchased from ULA. Amazon said launch carries risks, particularly on an inaugural mission, and expressed confidence that ULA would learn from the failure. The report describes Amazon Leo as a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink that has so far placed only a portion of its planned satellites in orbit.

content.headline: Worcestershire council considers 22 social-care job cuts as AI takes on admin
content.shortHeadline: Worcestershire council weighs social-care cuts as AI takes on admin
content.standfirst: Worcestershire County Council is consulting on cutting 22 full-time-equivalent roles in children’s and adult social care, with an AI transcription tool expected to handle some administration. The union says the case for replacing experienced staff needs evidence.

image.caption: Worcestershire deputy council leader Adam Kent.

sources.originalTitle: Why AI could replace 22 jobs in council social care

segments.body: Worcestershire County Council is consulting on cutting 22 full-time-equivalent jobs in children’s and adult social care. The council plans to use Beam Notes, an AI transcription tool, to turn meetings into structured reports and says the technology could help absorb administrative work.

segments.title: A dispute over safeguarding
segments.body: Unison says the roles at risk contribute to safeguarding, care management, case records and other statutory work. The union argues that replacing experienced staff with automation requires robust evidence and meaningful consultation. The council’s deputy leader says the tool can improve productivity and accuracy.

segments.title: Part of a wider savings plan
segments.body: The council faces a projected £98m budget gap next year and has proposed a wider transformation plan that could remove the equivalent of 100 jobs. In Hampshire, where Beam Notes is also used, the council estimates it has saved 3,000 staff days and increased productivity by 20% over the past year; those figures do not establish the tool’s impact in Worcestershire.

content.headline: Apple launches US study to test how people use AI for health advice
content.shortHeadline: Apple study will test how people use AI for health advice
content.standfirst: Apple is recruiting US participants to ask health questions through an app and rate its answers, in a study intended to inform future health tools. It is research into user experience, not evidence that the system is clinically effective.

sources.originalTitle: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health

segments.body: Apple has launched a study with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform, to examine how people use conversational AI for health questions and judge its responses. The app gives answers linked to clinical sources; participants can rate them for qualities such as accuracy, detail and relevance. The study aims to enrol up to 200,000 people in the US.

segments.title: Health data and privacy claims
segments.body: Participants may choose to share Apple Health data, such as activity, sleep or lab results, to provide more personal context. Apple says the information will remain confidential and will not be used to train AI models. TechCrunch reports that OpenEvidence deletes query and response data after 24 hours; these are company descriptions of the study’s data handling.

segments.title: Who can take part—and what the reports say
segments.body: Both reports describe US participants aged 21 or older, but differ on the device requirement: The Verge says an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 26 or later, while TechCrunch says an iPhone 15 or later and Apple Intelligence enabled. The Verge says the study app does not use Apple Intelligence, leaving the reported eligibility details unclear.

perspectives.body: The Verge reports that Apple’s study app does not use Apple Intelligence, despite TechCrunch reporting that the phone must have Apple Intelligence enabled. The sources also differ on the minimum iPhone model, so eligibility details are not fully consistent.

content.headline: England stun Spain 3-2 after 65 minutes of dominance in Madrid
content.shortHeadline: England stun Spain in a 3-2 Nations League thriller
content.standfirst: England led the world champions by three goals before Elliot Anderson’s sending-off sparked a tense finish. Thomas Tuchel’s side held on to claim a landmark win and top their Nations League group.

image.caption: James Trafford made key saves as England held off Spain’s late pressure.

sources.originalTitle: 60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages
How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

segments.body: England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid, ending the hosts’ 43-match unbeaten run apart from a penalty shootout defeat. Harry Kane’s penalty put England ahead, then Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored early in the second half to make it 3-0.

segments.title: The siege
segments.body: Elliot Anderson was sent off after fouling Lamine Yamal in the penalty area. Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the spot and Nico Williams made it 3-2, but England survived Spain’s late pressure. Tuchel said the team’s performance before the red card was a statement of its progress since the World Cup.

perspectives.body: BBC Sport’s comparison found Spain had 19 shots in the final 30 minutes, seven on target. James Trafford made six saves overall, including four in the final 12 minutes and a double stop in added time.

content.headline: McIlroy equals Montgomerie's record with eighth Race to Dubai title
content.shortHeadline: McIlroy matches Montgomerie's record with eighth Race to Dubai win
content.standfirst: McIlroy edged Eugenio Chacarra in the season-long standings to claim a fifth straight Race to Dubai title. He dedicated the record-equalling eighth to his father, Gerry, who is recovering from a double lung transplant.

image.caption: Rory McIlroy with his father, Gerry, at Augusta National.

sources.originalTitle: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

segments.body: Rory McIlroy matched Colin Montgomerie’s record of eight European Tour season-long titles after finishing runner-up at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai. He dedicated the Race to Dubai crown to his father, Gerry, who has been in hospital for two months following a double lung transplant.

segments.title: A close finish
segments.body: Tyrrell Hatton won the tournament by five shots, finishing on 15 under par. McIlroy closed with a bogey-free 67 to finish on 10 under and edge Chacarra for the season-long title. He said he hopes to move past Montgomerie’s record next year.

content.headline: Teenager Andreeva beats Svitolina to win WTA Finals on debut
content.shortHeadline: Andreeva wins WTA Finals on debut after beating Svitolina
content.standfirst: The 19-year-old Russian won 7-5 6-3 in the final, completing an unbeaten week without dropping a set. The title lifts her to second in the world rankings.

image.caption: Mirra Andreeva celebrates winning the WTA Finals.

sources.originalTitle: Teenager Andreeva caps stunning week with WTA Finals title

segments.body: Mirra Andreeva beat Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 to win the WTA Finals on her first appearance at the season-ending tournament. The 19-year-old, who won the French Open earlier this year, did not drop a set in her five matches.

segments.title: A breakthrough week
segments.body: Andreeva saved nine of the 12 break points she faced in the final and won three matches against top-10 opponents on the way to the title. She will begin 2027 ranked second in the world, 293 points behind Elena Rybakina.

content.headline: Wilson holds off Wakelin comeback to win first Champion of Champions title
content.shortHeadline: Wilson survives Wakelin fightback to win Champion of Champions
content.standfirst: Kyren Wilson was 9-3 ahead before Chris Wakelin fought back to within one frame. Wilson held on for a 10-8 win and a third consecutive tournament title.

sources.originalTitle: Wilson survives Wakelin comeback for third title

segments.body: Kyren Wilson beat Chris Wakelin 10-8 to win the Champion of Champions in Leicester, his first title at the event. Wilson led 9-3, but Wakelin’s breaks of 131, 57 and 50 brought him back to 9-8 before Wilson sealed the match with his fourth century break of the day.

segments.title: Three in a row
segments.body: The victory extends Wilson’s run to three consecutive titles, following wins at the Northern Ireland Open and International Championship. He is the first player to win three tournaments in a row since Judd Trump in 2023.

content.headline: Scotland edge Australia 15-12 in a defensive Murrayfield battle
content.shortHeadline: Scotland hold off Australia for 15-12 win
content.standfirst: Gregor Townsend praised one of Scotland’s best defensive displays in recent years after his side secured a narrow Nations Championship victory. Darcy Graham’s late tackle stopped Australia’s final attack.

sources.originalTitle: Townsend hails Scotland's defence in Australia 'arm wrestle'

segments.body: Scotland beat Australia 15-12 at Murrayfield in a low-scoring Nations Championship Test. Leading 12-5 at half-time, Scotland faced a late challenge after Max Jorgensen’s converted try brought the Wallabies within three points.

segments.title: Defence decides it
segments.body: With the clock in the red, Darcy Graham tackled Australia full-back Tom Wright into touch as the visitors attacked from their own half. Townsend praised Scotland’s physicality and discipline, saying their defence was among the best he had seen from the side in the past couple of years.

content.headline: Duncan wins first LPGA title after 222 events over 12 years
content.shortHeadline: Duncan claims first LPGA title after 222 attempts
content.standfirst: The American closed with a three-under-par 67 to win The Annika by two shots. Her first tour victory sends her into next week’s season-ending championship.

sources.originalTitle: First win for Duncan after 12 years & 222 attempts

segments.body: Lindy Duncan won her first LPGA Tour title at the 222nd attempt, finishing two shots clear of South Korea’s Choi Hye-jin at The Annika in Florida. Duncan’s three-under-par final round of 67 took her to 16 under.

The 35-year-old, who joined the tour in 2014, said she was “completely shocked” by the win. It also lifted her from 74th to 34th in the season-long standings, securing her place in next week’s 60-player finale.

content.headline: Ronaldinho returns at 46 as Ravenna beat Forli in Serie C derby
content.shortHeadline: Ronaldinho makes comeback at 46 in Ravenna win
content.standfirst: The former Brazil and Barcelona star came out of retirement to play the first half for Ravenna, where he is an investor. He helped build the move for the opening goal in a 2-0 victory.

image.caption: Ronaldinho played the first half for Ravenna against Forli.

sources.originalTitle: Ronaldinho makes comeback in Ravenna win

segments.body: Ronaldinho made his playing comeback at 46 as Ravenna beat Forli 2-0 in an Italian Serie C derby. He started and played the first half, making his first appearance since 2015, when he last played for Fluminense.

segments.title: A hand in the opener
segments.body: The former Barcelona player held off a defender and passed the ball in the move that led to Giulio Donati’s opening goal. Ronaldinho joined Ravenna as an investor in August and said he would return to play if the club’s president called him.

content.headline: Crash survivor Ruschel earns promotion in final game before retirement
content.shortHeadline: Ruschel retires after helping Juventude win promotion
content.standfirst: Alan Ruschel came off the bench in Juventude’s 2-0 win that secured promotion to Brazil’s top flight. The 37-year-old, one of six survivors of the 2016 Chapecoense plane crash, is retiring after the match.

sources.originalTitle: Chapecoense air crash survivor wins promotion in final game

segments.body: Alan Ruschel’s final match as a professional ended with Juventude securing promotion to Brazil’s Serie A. The 37-year-old came on in the 74th minute of a 2-0 win over Botafogo, then took part in an emotional farewell at the stadium.

segments.title: A return to football
segments.body: Ruschel was one of six survivors of the 2016 plane crash that killed 71 people, including 19 members of the Chapecoense team and its coaching staff. Despite severe injuries and spinal surgery, he returned to football a year later. He said he was retiring after two consecutive knee surgeries.
